page_title: How to Use Data Science to Understand What Makes Wine Taste Good

summary.title: How to Use Data Science to Understand What Makes Wine Taste Good
summary.one_liner: You learn to explore a wine quality dataset in Python (pandas, seaborn, scikit-learn setup) using statistics, correlation heatmaps, and Tukey's IQR method to find outliers.
keywords: uci machine learning repository wine data
how to find outliers in a dataset
predict wine quality with machine learning
vinho verde red and white wine
takeaways: How to load the UCI red wine CSV with pandas, check for missing values, and summarize statistics.
How to read correlation heatmaps and scatter plots to spot relationships between chemical features and wine quality.
What key wine chemistry terms (fixed/volatile acidity, residual sugar, pH, sulphates, alcohol) mean and how they relate to taste.
How Tukey's method (Q1, Q3, 1.5 x IQR) flags outliers, and why medians can be more robust than means.
summary.summary: This tutorial, by Ashwin Hariharan, walks through exploratory data analysis on the UCI red and white Vinho Verde wine datasets using Python in a Jupyter notebook. It covers loading and inspecting the data with pandas, grouping wines by quality rating, and explaining wine chemistry terms alongside the features. It then uses scatter matrices, correlation heatmaps, and seaborn joint plots to examine relationships such as pH vs. fixed acidity and alcohol vs. quality, followed by outlier detection with Tukey's IQR method. The machine learning classifier is promised for a follow-up post and is not covered here.
